$comment: Destructive-DDL gate allowlist (issue #91). Scope is DATA safety: the gate (scripts/verify-no-destructive-ddl.mjs) fails the build if any supabase/migrations/*.sql contains a data-destroying statement — DROP TABLE, ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN, DELETE (FROM), or TRUNCATE (incl. IF EXISTS variants) — that is NOT listed here. Each key is a migration filename; its value is the list of data-destroying operations REVIEWED and INTENTIONALLY permitted in that file, using the gate's canonical op names (DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, DELETE, TRUNCATE). The override is deliberately per-file + per-operation so every exception is auditable. Data safety is prioritized over convenience: a de-duplication migration must take an explicit entry here, never a loosening of the rule. DROP FUNCTION / DROP INDEX, REVOKE, and ALTER ... DROP DEFAULT / DROP CONSTRAINT destroy no data and are NOT gated, so they never need an entry. 012_prune_game_history.sql (LLD 149) has one intentional retention DELETE on game_history, allowlisted below.
